subject: CTH
body: Under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, employees must
options: write the site risk assessment themselves
follow only the instructions they agree with
take reasonable care of themselves and others affected by their work
provide their own PPE at their own cost
explanation: Section 7 also requires employees to co-operate with their employer on health and safety.

subject: CTH
body: Who must provide PPE needed for the job, free of charge?
explanation: Employers can't charge workers for PPE required for their work.

subject: CTH
body: A method statement explains
options: which tools are cheapest to buy
the site's opening and closing times
who will be paid for the task
how a task will be carried out safely, step by step
explanation: Read and follow the method statement; ask if anything isn't clear.

subject: CTH
body: If you think a method statement is unsafe for the conditions on site, you should
options: carry on and mention it at the end of the week
stop and tell your supervisor before carrying on
ask another operative to do the task instead
change the method yourself without telling anyone
explanation: Work must stop until the risk has been reviewed.

subject: CTH
body: An HSE inspector can issue a prohibition notice, which means
options: the company must pay a fine on the spot
the activity must stop until the danger is put right
the work can continue for 21 days
explanation: An improvement notice gives a deadline to fix a breach.

subject: CTH
body: Under RIDDOR, an injury that keeps a worker off normal duties for more than 7 days must be reported within
explanation: Deaths and specified injuries must be reported without delay.

subject: CTH
body: A near miss is
options: an event that could have caused injury or damage but didn't
an accident that caused minor injury
explanation: Reporting near misses helps prevent the next accident.

subject: CTH
body: Construction sites must provide welfare facilities including
options: a canteen with free hot meals
toilets, washing facilities, drinking water and a rest area
private car parking for every worker
a gym and showers for each trade
explanation: Facilities must be available from the start of the job.

subject: CTH
body: Which disease can be caused by breathing in asbestos fibres?
explanation: Asbestos-related diseases often appear 20 or more years after exposure.

subject: CTH
body: Asbestos is most likely to be found in buildings
options: built or refurbished before the year 2000
explanation: If you suspect asbestos, stop work and report it.

subject: CTH
body: Weil's disease (leptospirosis) is spread mainly through
options: contact with water or soil contaminated by rat urine
explanation: Cover cuts and wash hands before eating or smoking.

subject: CTH
body: Cutting concrete or stone creates a dust that can cause serious lung disease. The dust is
explanation: Use water suppression or extraction and suitable RPE.

subject: CTH
body: Tight-fitting respiratory protective equipment (RPE) will only protect you properly if it has been
options: worn for at least a full year
face-fit tested for you and you are clean-shaven where it seals
explanation: Stubble breaks the seal on the face.

subject: CTH
body: Contact dermatitis on construction sites is commonly caused by
options: wet cement and some resins or solvents
explanation: Wear suitable gloves and wash skin promptly.

subject: CTH
body: The upper exposure action value for daily noise exposure is
explanation: At 85 dB(A) hearing protection must be worn; at 80 dB(A) it must be made available.

subject: CTH
body: A sign that noise levels may be too high is that you
options: can hear a radio across the room
have to shout to be heard by someone 2 metres away
can talk normally at arm's length
explanation: Noise damage to hearing is permanent.

subject: CTH
body: Hand-arm vibration syndrome (HAVS) can cause
explanation: Limit trigger time and use low-vibration tools.

subject: CTH
body: Before lifting a load manually, you should first
options: consider whether a mechanical aid can be used instead
twist your back to reach it
lift it quickly to save time
ask the lightest person to carry it
explanation: Avoid hazardous manual handling where reasonably practicable.

subject: CTH
body: When lifting a load, you should keep it
options: at arm's length from your body
close to your waist with a firm grip
explanation: Bend your knees and avoid twisting.

subject: CTH
body: The first step in the work at height hierarchy is to
options: avoid working at height where possible
explanation: Then prevent falls, then minimise the distance and consequences of a fall.

subject: CTH
body: A leaning ladder should be set at an angle of about
options: 45 degrees, or 1 out for every 1 up
60 degrees, or 1 out for every 2 up
75 degrees, or 1 out for every 4 up
explanation: Make sure it is secured and on firm, level ground.

subject: CTH
body: Ladders are suitable for
options: short-duration, light work where a safer option isn't justified
carrying sheet materials up a roof
any job as long as it is under 10 metres
explanation: Short duration is generally taken as up to about 30 minutes in one position.

subject: CTH
body: A mobile tower scaffold should only be moved when
options: nobody and nothing is on the platform
one person is still on it to keep it steady
explanation: Check the brakes are on again before anyone climbs back up.

subject: CTH
body: A scaffold must be inspected
options: only when it is first erected
before first use, at least every 7 days, and after anything that could affect it
only after it has been dismantled
explanation: Look for a scaffold tag showing it's safe to use.

subject: CTH
body: Fragile roof materials such as old cement sheets and roof lights
options: are safe if you walk on the bolts
can be crossed if you move quickly
can give way under your weight without warning
explanation: Use staging and protection; never walk directly on them.

subject: CTH
body: Before digging, the main way to find buried services such as cables and pipes is to
options: dig quickly with a mechanical excavator
check service plans and use a cable avoidance tool (CAT)
explanation: Hand-dig trial holes to expose services.

subject: CTH
body: Excavations must be inspected
options: only if someone has been injured
only when the trench is finished
at the start of each shift and after any event that could affect stability
explanation: A competent person carries out inspections.

subject: CTH
body: Spoil and materials should be kept
options: back from the edge of an excavation
right on the edge of the trench
explanation: Loads near the edge can cause a collapse.

subject: CTH
body: Most deaths involving site vehicles happen while
explanation: Use a trained signaller (banksman) and keep out of reversing areas.

subject: CTH
body: You should only operate site plant if you are
options: over 18 and have a car licence
in a hurry and the driver is busy
trained, competent and authorised to use it
explanation: Never ride on plant unless a proper seat is provided.

subject: CTH
body: To be safe around moving plant, you should
options: make eye contact with the driver and keep out of the danger zone
rely on hearing the reversing alarm
explanation: Use segregated pedestrian routes.

subject: CTH
body: Portable electric tools on UK construction sites should normally run on
options: 110 volts supplied through a reduced-voltage transformer
explanation: Battery-powered tools are safer still.

subject: CTH
body: Before using an electrical tool, you should
options: tape over any cuts in the cable
run the cable through standing water
check the cable, plug and casing for damage
explanation: Don't use damaged equipment; report it.

subject: CTH
body: If you find an overhead power line near your work area, you should
options: lift scaffold tubes under it carefully
stop and get advice on safe distances and barriers
use a wooden ladder to get closer
explanation: Contact with overhead lines kills.

subject: CTH
body: The three sides of the fire triangle are
explanation: Remove one side and the fire goes out.

subject: CTH
body: Which extinguisher should be used on a fire involving live electrical equipment?
explanation: Water conducts electricity.

subject: CTH
body: Hot works such as welding or grinding near flammable materials normally need
options: a hot work permit and a fire watch afterwards
the area to be wet with petrol
explanation: Fire can smoulder for some time after work stops.

subject: CTH
body: A blue circular sign means
options: you must do something, such as wear a hard hat
a safe condition such as a first aid point
explanation: Red circles prohibit; yellow triangles warn; green signs show safe conditions.

subject: CTH
body: A green rectangular sign usually shows
options: a safe condition, such as a fire exit or first aid
explanation: Fire-fighting equipment signs are red.

subject: CTH
body: A yellow triangular sign with a black border means
explanation: For example, overhead loads or electricity.

subject: CTH
body: COSHH regulations deal with
options: substances hazardous to health such as chemicals and dusts
explanation: Read the safety data sheet and COSHH assessment.

subject: CTH
body: A red diamond-shaped symbol with a black skull and crossbones means a substance is
explanation: Follow the controls in the COSHH assessment.

subject: CTH
body: Where should you find information on the hazards of a chemical product?
options: the safety data sheet and the product label
explanation: Ask your supervisor for the COSHH assessment.

subject: CTH
body: Work in a confined space such as a manhole or tank needs
options: no special controls if it's short
a permit to work and a rescue plan before entry
explanation: Dangerous gases and lack of oxygen can kill quickly.

subject: CTH
body: If oil or diesel is spilt near a surface water drain, you should first
options: cover it with soil and leave it
carry on and report it later
wash it into the drain with water
stop the source if safe and protect the drain with a spill kit
explanation: Then report the spill.

subject: CTH
body: Site waste should be
options: segregated into the right skips so it can be recycled or disposed of properly
mixed in one skip to save space
explanation: Hazardous waste needs special handling.

subject: CTH
body: A site induction tells you about
options: site hazards, rules, welfare and emergency arrangements
how to apply for a mortgage
explanation: You must attend before starting work.

subject: CTH
body: Being under the influence of drugs or alcohol at work is dangerous because
options: it slows reactions and affects judgement
explanation: Most sites have a zero-tolerance policy and test workers.

subject: CTH
body: Toolbox talks are
options: short safety briefings on a specific topic or task
explanation: Ask questions if anything is unclear.

subject: CTH
body: If you find an injured person on site, you should first
options: make sure the area is safe and call for a first aider
leave them and finish your work
explanation: Call 999 for serious injuries.
